title: Altering planarian voltage patterns changes head number and head species-shape

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Altering planarian voltage patterns changes head number and head species-shape

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In planaria, manipulating the endogenous bioelectric voltage pattern by targeting gap junctions or ion channels can produce worms with one, two or zero heads, or with head and brain shapes resembling other extant planarian species.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Manipulation of the normal voltage pattern by targeting the gap junctions (Sordillo and Bargmann, 2021) or ion channels can give rise to planaria with one, two, or 0 heads, or heads with shape (and brain shape) resembling other extant species of planaria (Emmons-Bell et al., 2015; Sullivan et al., 2016).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops”. Scope: Regenerating planarian fragments (e.g. Dugesia japonica) treated with gap-junction or ion-channel modulators

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head number and shape changes are direct, discriminating endpoints with multiple published experiments. Open reports can resolve demonstrated cases, but complete raw data and mechanistic specificity remain limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare head count, head outline, brain morphology, and voltage maps after gap-junction or ion-channel perturbation with vehicle controls and reference species using blinded image classification.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Drug treatments can have off-target effects.

Resemblance to another species depends on the morphometric classifier.

Raw images and voltage measurements may be incomplete.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.72
data existence: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head number and morphometric distance to reference species are standard variables, and several papers publish counts for gap-junction and channel perturbations in regenerating planaria. Planform compiles literature experiments of this kind, while the underlying images and landmarks remain in the papers. The phenotypic claim can be audited for the reported species and manipulations, short of an independent raw-data reanalysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count heads, and compare head and brain landmarks to reference species, after gap-junction or ion-channel perturbation versus vehicle; the claim holds if one, two, and zero heads, and non-native head shapes, occur above the vehicle rate.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Toxicity can change head number unless vehicle and washout controls are carried along.

Planform encodes published outcomes and may omit landmark-level shapes from later papers.

Most quantitative series come from one laboratory, and raw images are not in a measurement archive.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.8
